 Order
With the consent of both the parties, matter is heard finally.

02. The appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") being aggrieved by the amount awarded in claim case No.1310/2017 vide award dated 05.02.2020 passed by the Fourth Additional Member, MACT,
Indore (M.P.), whereby an amount of compensation of Rs.10,42,604/- has been awarded to the respondent.
03. The relevant and necessary facts of the case are that on 23.12.2016, claimant / injured Ravi was sitting in offending Loading Rickshaw bearing registration No.MP-09-LQ-5511 alongwith water jars.
The offending vehicle was being driven by the respondent No.2 Sanjay and due to his negligence it over turned and due to which Ravi sustained grievous injuries.
He was admitted in the Verma Union Hospital, an iron rod / plate was implicated in his legs through operation.
Matter has been reported by him in P.S. Palasia, respondent No.1 is the owner of the said vehicle.
Offending Vehicle was insured with the respondent No.3 at the time of accident.

2 MA-2828-2020 04. Respondent No.1 / claimant has preferred a claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act before the below Tribunal by submitting that Rs.4,00,000/- has been spent in his treatment and due to the injury sustained in the aforesaid accident, he became unable to perform any work from his left hand.

As per the disability certificate issued by the District Medical Board, he has sustained 60%

1 permanent disability.

sentences.text: He was working as a Helper in the offending vehicle and earned more than Rs.9,000/- per month.
Hence, it is prayed that he should be awarded Rs.30,00,000/- with interest.
05. Respondent Nos.2 and 3 both were remained ex-parte before the below Tribunal.

06. Appellant / Insurance Company denied all the claim averments by submitting in its written statement that at the time of incident, respondent No.2 was not having any valid and effective license and aforesaid vehicle was used after violating the terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
FIR is also belated.
Victim was traveling in a loading vehicle and no extra premium has been paid for him, therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable for any compensation.

07. On the basis of the aforesaid pleadings, the below Tribunal has framed the issues and after recording and appreciating the evidence available on record, partly allowed the claim petition and compensation of Rs.10,42,604/- with interest @ 6% per annum has been awarded.
Being aggrieved by the same, appellant Insurance Company has preferred this appeal.

08. Counsel for the appellant contended that the impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is against the law and fact, below Tribunal has ignored the pleadings and the evidence adduced by the appellant, vehicle was insured as a goods vehicle and was manufactured only for the purpose of carrying the goods, 3 MA-2828-2020 but injured was sitting in the back portion of the goods vehicle as a passenger, he has to be treated as gratuitous passenger and no premium was charged by the appellant for such type of passenger.
Terms and conditions of the insurance policy has been violated, therefore, the Insurance Company is not liable for compensation.
Below Tribunal has ignored all these facts hence, he prays that impugned order be set aside.

09. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by submitting that impugned award passed by the below Tribunal is just, proper and adequate and not deserves for any interference.
10. Nobody appeared on behalf of the respondent Nos.2 and 3, despite service of notice.
11. Both the parties heard at length and perused the entire record with due care.

12. Claimant Ravi (PW/1) deposed before the below Tribunal that at the time of incident, he was going to Saket Chouraha by Loading Rickshaw bearing registration No.MP-09-LQ-5511 with water cans because he was working as a Helper in the loading vehicle, but in his cross-examination he admits that he did not produce any relevant document that he was working as a Helper in the offending vehicle, he did not mention his employer's name in the claim petition.
13. Although, his statement is supported by Nilesh Jain (PW/2), but Nilesh Jain also admits in his cross-examination that he saw the incident.
Injured was traveling in the Loading Richshaw with the water cans.

Appellant has examined Divya Mishra (DW/1) before the below Tribunal, she categorically stated that offending vehicle was insured with the appellant Insurance Company and the insurance policy is Exhibit D/1 which has been issued for goods carrier, but as per the policy, no Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Ravi on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180904918/
2 risk was covered by the Insurance Company for the passenger who 4 MA-2828-2020 was traveling in the loading part of the vehicle and no extra premium was paid by the vehicle owner to the Insurance Company.

sentences.text:
14. On the basis of the aforesaid evidence, it is admitted that the injured was gratuitous passenger in the goods vehicle, vehicle was insured as per the insurance police (Exhibit D/1) as a goods vehicle,
the vehicle was not build for carrying the passengers, whereas the claimant / insured was sitting in the back portion (loading part) of the goods vehicle, therefore, he has to be treated as gratuitous passenger and accordingly it is a clear cut violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy (Exhibit D/1), therefore, on the basis of the breach of the insurance policy, the appellant is not liable to pay the compensation amount.

15. Claimant has failed to prove that he was working as a Helper in the aforesaid vehicle, owner of vehicle was not examined by the claimant, no relevant document has been produced to establish that the claimant was in employment of the owner of the offending vehicle as a Helper.
Hence, the claimant has failed to prove that he was a Helper in the aforesaid vehicle.

16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mithlesh & others V/s Brijendra Singh Baghel & others reported in 2007 ACJ 10 in para 7 has held as under:
''7.

entities.text: Mithlesh & others V/s Brijendra Singh Baghel & others reported in 2007 ACJ 10
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, from the aforesaid evidence on record, it is clear that the tractor was insured for agricultural purpose and at the relevant time the same was not being used for agricultural purposes.
It is not the case of the appellants that the owner or his representative was travelling on the vehicle along with the goods.

Therefore, from the aforesaid discussion it is clear that the insurance company is not liable for payment of any compensation as the liability of the deceased is not covered under the policy and more so it is not the case of third party risk as the deceased was not third party."
17.
Admittedly, in this case, except driver of the Loading Rickshaw, no one was covered with the insurance policy.

Claimant has failed to prove that he was traveling in the offending vehicle as a Helper, therefore, the terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated and the Insurance Company is not liable to 5 MA-2828-2020 pay the compensation.

18. Hence, the impugned award dated 05.02.2020 passed by the Fourth Additional Member, MACT,
Indore (M.P.) is modified and the direction given in paragraph No.37 of the impugned award is hereby set aside.
Rest of the award is maintained.
19. With the aforesaid, this Misc. Appeal is disposed of .
No order as to the cost.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Divyansh Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. Ltd. vs Ravi on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/180904918/
